content.summary_of_the_paper: -This paper studies the problem of learning with noisy (weak) labels without any clean data. To solve this problem, they propose to jointly learn a classification model and a label correction model with a shared feature extractor, and a combined learning objective with a binary cross-entropy loss between the self-generated (soft) pseudo label and the corrected class posterior and a cross-entropy between the hard version of the pseudo label and the model predictions. The proposed method contains many heuristics, such as fixing the linear classifier (prediction head) after initialization, etc. They also provide some favorable experimental results in the paper.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:

-The paper is ambitious to solve the very general problem of weakly supervised learning. Although the proposed method contains many heuristics, it is shown to work well on many benchmark datasets.

Cons:

-The idea of jointly learning a classification model and a label correction rule in learning with noisy labels (and without any clean data) is not new. A highly related existing work on this has been missed, see 

Joint Optimization Framework for Learning with Noisy Labels, CVPR 2018

This work is the first one, to the best of my knowledge,  to propose a joint framework for learning the predictor and corrector. I suggest the authors carefully discuss this paper in related work and compare the proposed method with it in experiments.

-The problem setting of the current paper seems to be learning with noisy labels, rather than weakly supervised learning. The paper misuse weak labels which actually mean noisy (corrupted) labels. Weak supervision can be very general, including but not limited to inaccurate supervision, e.g., noisy labels; incomplete supervision, e.g., positive and unlabeled data; inexact supervision, e.g., similarities and dissimilarities…A recent book nicely summarises them, see

Machine Learning from Weak Supervision: An Empirical Risk Minimization Approach, MIT Press

Obviously, the proposed method cannot work with all kinds of weak supervision, I suggest the authors introduce weak supervision with its generality and then specifies the current paper targets a specific weakly supervised learning problem that deals with noisy labels.

-The proposed method includes training a predictor and a label corrector with a combined learning objective, where the predictor will be pretrained. A concern is that if the predictor is not trained well (e.g., trained for longer epochs and overfits to the noisy labels), the generated pseudo labels may not be reliable, and in worse cases, they may even be harmful to further training, how can we make sure the proposed method can converge?

-Another concern is the trick that the predictor $h_\text{pred}$ is fixed after initialization, if this helps improve performance, my hypothesis is that $h_\text{pred}$ is already well trained during initialization, my question is how do we know that the initialization training is adequate? Can the authors provide more details about the initialization?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
-Clarity:

The paper is structured well and very easy to follow. However, the title may be misleading as it seems that the paper solves the very general problem of weakly supervised learning by the self-correction method, which is not really true. See the detailed comments above.

-Quality:

-The paper proposes a joint learning approach for learning with noisy labels, although the proposed method has many heuristics, it is shown to work well on benchmark datasets.

-Novelty:

-A highly related work has been missing in this paper, which should be discussed and compared with.

-Reproducibility: good
content.summary_of_the_review: -Overall the paper considers a practically useful problem, but the presentation needs to be improved, see the detailed comments above.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper targets a research problem that how to improve the robustness of learning models when datasets contain label errors. To solve the problem, a new label-correction based method has been proposed.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

+ The research problem is important and may have many practical applications. The real-world machine learning dataset can easily contain label errors. Improving the generalization of learning models trained on noisy data is important.

+ This paper generally is well structured and easy to follow. 

Weakness:
+ The technical insight may not be enough, a lot of label-selection and label-correction based methods have been proposed for learning with label errors. It is not clear what is the advantage of the proposed method theoretically. I think it is better to add some insightful analysis.
+ the probability $P(Y|\tilde{Y},X)$ in general cannot be identified without clean labels. The authors should add some discussion that how to identify the probability $P(Y|\tilde{Y},X)$ and, what assumptions are required.
+ Missing a lot of important baselines and datasets. A lot of methods for learning with label errors should be compared (e.g., JoCoR, CVPR’20; DivideMix, CVPR’20; MEIDTM, CVPR’22). The benchmark datasets such as CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and Clothing1M should also be compared.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper leverages label-selection and correction for label-learning with label errors. These two techniques have been well studied. The written quality overall is good.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper focuses on a practical research problem. My largest concern is that the technical insight may not be that strong and the experiments are insufficient.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors study one of the tasks from weakly supervised learning which supervision is inaccurate. Facing with noisy annotation, previous works try to identify the possibly wrong annotations and filter or downweight those annotations. Instead of getting rid of them, the author proposes a predictor-corrector structure network and tries to correct the wrong predictions.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength：
The insight is easy to understand and the work is relatively easy to follow.

Weakness:
The description of the target task is unspecific. In fact, there are kinds of weak supervision, not only the labels may contain noise. E.g. low level label for high level task, like class label for localization \cite[CAM]. The author does not clarify what kind of weak supervision they are dealing with until the method part.

[CAM]: (2016CVPR)Learning Deep Features for Discriminative Localization

The comparison methods are not fresh. Only COSINE is from NAACL21. Then the next method is from the year of 20. The author should compare with some more 2022 methods.

I have a little concerned about the effectivity and novelty part. For effectivity part, the author puts most efforts on describing what their method like rather than explain why their corrector can correct the wrong annotations which I believe is their key contribution. For example, in formula 2, I can understand that they remodel the multi-class classification into binary classification. But why binary classification better than multi-class classification since there is no extra priori knowledge involved. For the novelty part, as the authors state in the method part, ‘Fixed predictor’ and ‘Pseudo label generation’ has been used in prior works, so these are just tricks and the authors just follow the previous works?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
This paper is well written and easy to follow.
In the experiments, the proposed method has been verified on several datasets.
The novelty of the paper should be further explained by comparing with the state-of-the-art methods.
content.summary_of_the_review: For classification task which contains noisy annotations. The authors propose to use a corrector to correct the wrong predictions from the predictor. The corrector and the predictor can be trained jointly and improved each other. The paper is easy to follow. I have some concerns about the novelty, the effectivity as well as the experimental comparison.

content.title: SELCOR: Self-Correction for Weakly Supervised Learning
content.TL;DR: We propose a self-training based method to reduce noise in weak labels for weakly supervised learning.
content.abstract: Powerful machine learning models often require training with large amounts of labeled data. Collecting precise labels from human supervision is expensive and time-consuming. Instead, it is much easier to obtain large-scale weak labels from multiple weak supervision sources such as rules or knowledge graphs, whereas weak labels could be noisy and make models prone to overfitting. We propose a self-training method for weakly supervised learning without using any true label. Our method learns a joint model with a corrector and a predictor, where the predictor generates pseudo clean labels and the corrector revises weak labels to reproduces the pseudo labels generated by the predictor. The joint model is trained by encouraging consistency between label generation and label correction, such that the predictor and corrector can iteratively improve each other to generate more reliable pseudo label for self-training. In this way, our method makes full use of weak labels and effectively suppresses label noise in weak labels and pseudo labels. Experiments on 8 benchmark datasets show that our method outperforms existing weakly supervised methods by large margins.
